message.content:
Determining the “best” jazz singer is highly subjective and depends on personal taste, era, and style. However, several artists are frequently cited as the most influential and celebrated:

| Singer | Notable Contributions | Why They’re Often Mentioned |
|--------|-----------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Billie Holiday** | Pioneered emotive phrasing and storytelling in jazz vocals. | Her unique phrasing and emotional depth set a new standard for vocal jazz. |
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” she mastered scat singing and impeccable diction. | Her technical mastery and versatility across many styles earned her universal acclaim. |
| **Sarah Vaughan** | Possessed a wide vocal range and rich tone, blending jazz with pop and blues. | Her vocal agility and expressive phrasing made her a benchmark for jazz singers. |
| **Nat King Cole** | Combined smooth baritone with sophisticated arrangements. | His crossover appeal and lyrical delivery helped bring jazz to a broader audience. |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | Modern reinterpretations of standards with a deep, smoky voice. | Her innovative approach keeps jazz fresh and relevant. |

If you’re looking for a definitive “best,” it’s often a matter of which qualities—technical skill, emotional impact, innovation—you value most. Each of the singers above has left an indelible mark on the genre.
